paper_sections.title: Conscious and unconscious brain responses to food and cocaine cues
Main effect of time of day

description.value: The study assessed fMRI responses to food, cocaine, and neutral visual cues presented subliminally or supraliminally, and tested whether cue reactivity varied between morning and evening sessions.

design.value: Sixteen healthy, cocaine-naïve volunteers completed randomly ordered fMRI sessions in the morning and evening. Across three presentation-time sessions, food, cocaine, and neutral cues were presented in an event-related design for 33, 750, or 3000 ms.

name.value: Structured Clinical Interview for the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-IV)

description.value: Used to assess drug abuse or dependence and neurological or psychiatric disorders, including eating disorders such as binge eating.
Participants rated “How negative/positive do you find the picture?” from -3 (very negative) to 3 (very positive).
Participants rated “How much does the picture excite you?” from 0 (not at all) to 6 (extremely).
Participants rated “How much do you want to consume the depicted item right now?” from 0 (not at all) to 6 (extremely).
Participants self-reported hunger levels before and after the scanning sessions on a 7-point Likert scale.
Participants were instructed to press a button if they saw an animal to ensure that they were paying attention.

source_definition.value: Six realignment parameters were included as regressors of no interest.

description.value: Healthy, cocaine-naïve volunteers without drug abuse or dependence, neurological or psychiatric disorders, eating disorders, major medical problems, psychoactive medication use, or ferromagnetic implants.

excluded_count.value: Two participants had excessive head motion during their MRI scans (>2 mm), resulting in n=14 participants for further fMRI analyses.

inclusion_criteria.value: Participants were naïve to cocaine use.

exclusion_criteria.value: ferromagnetic implants, psychoactive medications and major medical problems, presence of drug abuse or dependence, and neurological or psychiatric disorders (including eating disorders such as binge eating)

medical_condition.value: healthy; no major medical problems, drug abuse or dependence, neurological or psychiatric disorders, or eating disorders

diagnostic_system.value: Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-IV)

diagnostic_instrument.value: Structured Clinical Interview for the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-IV)

medication_status.value: Participants were screened to exclude psychoactive medications.

task_description.value: A total of 40 appetitive food, 40 cocaine-related and 40 neutral images were presented in a randomized order in an event-related design. Each participant performed the three presentation-time sessions twice on two separate days, once between 9 and 11 AM and once between 5 and 7 PM, in randomized order.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to press a button if they saw an animal.

stimuli.value: Appetitive high- and low-calorie foods, cocaine-related images, and neutral images from the International Affective Picture System and in-house picture libraries; picture groups were matched for luminance.

task_performance_measures.value: button press if an animal was seen
subjective valence, arousal, and wanting ratings
self-reported hunger levels before and after scanning

instrument.value: 3 T Magnetom Prisma scanner (Siemens Medical Solutions USA, Inc., Malvern, PA), with a 32-channel head coil

description.value: A standard echo planar imaging (EPI) sequence was used with sequential interleaved acquisition, 64×64 pixels in-plane resolution, 36 slices, slice thickness 4 mm, voxel dimensions 3×3×4 mm3, and field of view 192×192 mm2.

Functional data were slice-time corrected, spatially realigned, co-registered to the T1 structural images, normalized to the Montreal Neurological Institute template, and smoothed with a 6 mm full-width at half-maximum Gaussian kernel.

software.value: SPM8 (Wellcome Department of Cognitive Neurology, London, UK)

steps.value: co-registration to the T1 structural images
normalization to the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) template
smoothing with a 6 mm full-width at half-maximum Gaussian kernel

hrf_model.value: hemodynamic response function with default temporal filtering of 128 s

model_settings.value: For every participant and each session, three fMRI regressors—food, cocaine, and neutral events—were created and convolved with the hemodynamic response function. Six realignment parameters were included as regressors of no interest. Single-subject contrasts were food>neutral, food>cocaine, and cocaine>neutral.

The first-level contrast images were entered with presentation time (33, 750 and 3000 ms) and time of day (am and pm) as within-subject factors. Whole-brain analyses used p<0.005 uncorrected at the voxel level, family-wise error corrected pFWE<0.05 at the cluster level, and minimum cluster size k>100; coordinates were reported in MNI space.

description.value: Appetitive high- and low-calorie food images, including savory and sweet breakfast and dinner items.
Cocaine-related images including bags of cocaine, lines of cocaine on a table, cocaine in spoons, cocaine pipes, and people smoking cocaine.
Neutral items from IAPS and in-house picture libraries.
Subliminal cue presentation for 33 ms, followed by a 467 ms neutral mask.
Supraliminal cue presentation for 750 ms without backward masking.
Supraliminal cue presentation for 3000 ms without backward masking.

definition.value: food > neutral contrast for the 3000 ms presentation time
food > neutral contrast for the 33 ms presentation time
food > neutral contrast for the 750 ms presentation time
food > neutral cues (all presentation times included)

interpretations.value: increased visual attention for food cues over all presentation times

description.value: Provides whole brain activations for the food > neutral contrast for each presentation time separately (33, 750, and 3000 ms), at an exploratory threshold of 0.005 uncorrected k>20.
